subject: Re: AcmeCorp BCP & multi-region switchover sequencing — questions

Subject: AcmeCorp BCP questionnaire: sequencing and realistic switchover times

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our RFP evaluation we need a more prescriptive sequencing and timing estimate for multi-region failover for Redwood Inference. Specifically, can you provide: 

- An ordered runbook for a primary->secondary region switchover (including pre-cutover checks, traffic shifting, KV/cache warmup, post-cutover validation).
- Expected RTO and RPO for our typical ML inference workloads (we average 1.2k QPS, median seq len 512 tokens).
- DNS cutover guidance (TTL values, phased cutover vs immediate) and any recommended infra changes on our side.
- Any assumptions (e.g., warm standby vs cold start, pre-warmed caches) that materially change estimates.

We will need a document we can share with our SREs and legal. If you have a runbook or playbook draft, please attach. Also include any test/validation checklists and recent test windows you can support.

Best,
Emily Novak
Sourcing Lead, AcmeCorp

--

Emily — thanks for the clear ask. We're attaching a targeted runbook draft and a network diagram to kick things off (redwood-runbook-acme-v1.pdf, network-diagram-acme.png). High-level answers up front so you have something to share with your SREs immediately: 

- Recommended mode: warm-standby for predictable RTO at your scale. Active-active is possible but requires additional cross-region networking and affinity controls.
- Typical RTO (warm standby, pre-warmed model instances & KV cache primed): 3–7 minutes for control-plane and DNS cutover; 5–15 minutes end-to-end for traffic stabilization depending on DNS TTL and client retry behavior.
- Typical RPO: near-zero for request data if you use our request-replay/streaming ack pipeline; otherwise last-successful-state window 30s–2m depending on replication settings.
- DNS guidance: use short TTL (30–60s) for failover windows; phased cutover (canary to 10% -> 50% -> 100%) reduces risk.

Quick ask: do you want us to assume your VPC peering and cross-region networking are already provisioned, or should we include network provisioning steps? I’ll loop Laura for the detailed sequencing and KV warmup specifics.

Thanks — attaching runbook (see attachments).

Best,
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Ben/Team — quick follow-up from our SREs after reviewing the draft. A few technical clarifications we need before we can sign off on warm-standby: 

1) KV cache warmup: do you pre-populate KV cache in the standby region from snapshot replication, or is the cache rebuilt on first access? If it’s snapshot-based, what is the expected warmup time for a working set of ~150GB?

2) DNS and client behavior: our clients honor DNS TTL but some legacy clients have 5m caching regardless of TTL. Do you have recommendations for handling client-side caching during the window?

3) Cutover automation: can your orchestration reproduce the canary->full step automatically, and do you provide vetting hooks (smoke tests) before promoting traffic?

We'd like to schedule a short technical call with your infra lead to walk through the runbook and network diagram next week. 

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, AcmeCorp
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@acmecorp.com>, Emily Novak <emily.novak@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AcmeCorp BCP questionnaire: sequencing and realistic switchover times

Carlos/Emily — Laura from Redwood infra here. Thanks for the precise questions; answers below and notes on assumptions. I captured this as a short Q&A so your SREs can paste into their runbook.

Q1 — KV cache warmup: 
- We support two modes: 1) snapshot-based seeding: we snapshot the hot working set from primary and transfer to standby (recommended for your ~150GB working set). In our tests, transfer+load for 150GB across a 10Gb link is typically 6–12 minutes depending on available bandwidth and compression. 2) on-demand rebuild: cache populates on first access, which leads to uneven latency during initial minutes and can extend RTO by 10–30 minutes depending on traffic patterns.

Q2 — DNS/client caching: 
- If clients may ignore TTL, we recommend combining short TTLs (30–60s) with a connection-level retry strategy: issue a 503->retry hint and maintain a short-lived session cookie to steer rebalanced clients. For legacy clients with stubborn caching, an HTTP/edge-layer redirect (302 to new endpoint) during the canary window can help. We can add a temporary proxy route in the old region that forwards to the new region while DNS propagates.

Q3 — Cutover automation & vetting hooks: 
- Our orchestration supports scripted canary promotions (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with configurable wait periods and automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions. Hooks: smoke tests (latency P95, error-rate, model output sanity checks) are executed before each promotion step. You can define custom validators (webhook or lambda) to integrate with your internal health checks. 

Sequencing summary (condensed runbook):
1) Pre-cutover (T-30 to T-5 minutes): verify cross-region network, confirm snapshots in-flight, set target DNS TTL to 30s, roll warm instances in standby, and seed KV snapshot.
2) Canary (T0): route 10% traffic to standby, run smoke validators for 2–5 minutes.
3) Gradual ramp (T0+5m): 50% traffic for 5–10 minutes, validate metrics.
4) Full cutover (T0+15m): switch 100% traffic, keep proxy fallback for 10–30 minutes, monitor-for-60m, and then remove proxy.

Expected numbers (warm-standby, with snapshot seed and pre-warmed instances):
- RTO (control-plane & client-facing stabilization): 3–12 minutes (we use the conservative window of 15 minutes for SLA conversations).
- RPO: <= 1 minute with streaming replication enabled; otherwise explainable up to 2–3 minutes depending on replication window.

Attachments & evidence: the runbook draft we sent includes the step-by-step commands and smoke-test definitions. I also attached a SOC2 summary (soc2-summary.pdf) that details controls around backups and replication for audits.

Next steps: 
- We can schedule a 45-min technical run-through next week. Proposed times: Tue 2025-11-18 10:00 PST or Wed 2025-11-19 14:00 PST. Which works best?
